newsitem.title: USA: Three killed in Arizona plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in Arizona plane crash.

text.p: Three people in a small plane were killed on Thursday night when it hop-scotched across a runway at Scottsdale airport, striking two other unmanned planes, a fire department spokesman said.

The single-engine Mooney aircraft made a normal landing but suddenly accelerated, taking off again to a height of about 10 feet (3 metres) and hitting the tail fin of a small Cessna plane before veering into a larger CanadaAir corporate jet, Scottsdale Rural Metro Fire Department spokesman Colin Williams said.
"The Mooney embedded itself into one of the rear engines of the CanadaAir jet. From the looks of it the people in the Mooney died instantly," Williams said.

He said the plane had taken off from Casa Grande, Arizona, south of Phoenix, Arizona, and was believed to have been piloted by its owner. The names of the victims were being withheld pending notification of relatives.
The airport tower was manned at the time and fire crews were on the scene within 30 seconds of the incident, he said.
"There was no distress call from the Mooney and because the fire station was so close to where it happened, crews were there within 30 seconds and sprayed the whole area with foam," Williams said.
Officials from the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board were investigating the crash.
